newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Qatar negotiating LNG export deal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Qatar negotiating LNG export deal.

text.p: Qatar and the Suez Canal Authority said on Monday they were negotiating the terms of an agreement to export Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) via the strategic waterway to Europe.

Qatari Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah, who is visiting the canal, told reporters he had asked the Suez Canal Authority (SCA) for a bigger discount in transit fees for the LNG to "increase the product's competitiveness in the European markets."
"Depending on the deal we get from the SCA, we will decide on either exporting the LNG to Europe or to Asia," Attiyah said.
SCA head Ahmed Fadel also told reporters after meeting Attiyah that a technical committee was looking into drafting a long-term LNG export agreement with Qatar.

"Based on the results of the study, the SCA will give new discounts," Fadel said. "We will try and fulfil the demands of the Qatari firms as well as take into consideration the revenues of the canal."
The Suez Canal currently offers a 35 percent discount on the fees for LNG shipments.

On Friday, the London-based al-Hayat daily newspaper said the SCA would give Qatar an extra five to 10 percent discount if it sends between three and four million tonnes of gas a year through the canal.
